After any sequence of play calls, if the last call did not win (random == 1), pot equals the sum of all contributions; if the last call won (random == 0), pot equals 0. The buggy version never resets pot, so pot remains > 0 after a win the fuzzer can find.

After any sequence of play calls, the contract's pot balance must be congruent modulo TICKET_AMOUNT to the sum of net contributions (total paid in minus total paid out); the buggy version leaves pot with an extra remainder after a win.

After any call to play(), the pot balance is either 0 (if a win just occurred) or strictly greater than 0 (if no win just occurred), but never exactly FEE_AMOUNT (1); the buggy version can leave pot = 1 after a win, violating this invariant.

After any two consecutive play() calls where the first wins (random == 0) and the second loses (random == 1), the reference pot equals the second call's msg.value (10), while the buggy pot equals the second call's msg.value plus the pot leftover from the first win's payout (which is FEE_AMOUNT, 1).

After any call to play(), if the reverted random was 1 (no win), the pot must be strictly greater than 0; the buggy version fails to reset pot after a win, so a subsequent losing call can result in pot == 0.
After any play, if a win occurs the pot must become 0 and the bank balance must increase by FEE_AMOUNT, which the bug violates by never transferring funds.

After any call to play(), the sum of the pot and the bank balance remains at least the total tickets bought minus fees paid; the mutant can reduce the pot without transferring the fee to the bank, breaking this invariant.

After any call to play(), the contract's pot is less than or equal to the sum of all ETH sent to play(). The bug changes the randomness source, altering which inputs lead to pot reset; the invariant checks that pot never exceeds total received ETH, which reference always satisfies but the bug can violate under the same sequence of plays.

The invariant is that after any sequence of play() calls, address(c).balance equals c.pot(); the buggy mutant with a changed randomness source can cause a payout when pot is 0, making the contract balance less than pot and violating the invariant.

After any number of play calls by any actors, if play did not reset the pot (i.e., pot remains > 0), the contract balance equals pot; the mutant using block.number can cause a payout when the original would not reset, making balance less than pot.
After any sequence of play calls, the contract's ETH balance equals the sum of fees owed to the bank plus the pot; the mutant can pay out when it shouldn't, leaving the balance inconsistent with pot.

After any sequence of play calls by any actors, the contract ETH balance is always at least as large as the pot (because pot tracks collected tickets not yet paid out), respecting the invariant that the contract holds all deposits until a payout resets the pot. The buggy version changes the randomness source, allowing a payout to occur in some scenario where the reference would not, thus the balance may become less than the pot, violating this invariant.

The total pot tracked by the contract matches the actual Ether balance of the contract after any sequence of valid plays; the buggy % 3 causes a mismatch because the random condition triggers less frequently, accumulating a surplus balance not reflected in the pot.

The bank's balance never exceeds the FEE_AMOUNT after any number of plays because a win always transfers exactly FEE_AMOUNT to the bank and resets the pot; the %3 mutant breaks this by allowing a win after the pot has accumulated more than one ticket, leaving the bank with more than FEE_AMOUNT.

For any sequence of plays, the pot must equal zero immediately after a win occurs; the %3 mutant can leave the pot non-zero after a win because it can win when the pot has accumulated multiple tickets but only resets the pot instead of draining it completely.

For any play that results in a win, the contract's Ether balance is reduced by exactly the pot at the time of the play minus FEE_AMOUNT; the %3 mutant causes wins to occur with a different pot value, breaking this invariant.

For any play that wins, the sum of bank and msg.sender receives exactly pot before the win; the %3 mutant lets the win occur when pot has multiple tickets but only resets pot instead of draining it, breaking the conservation.
